text: Five thousand three hundred years ago, a man climbed an alpine pass, and never came down.
He carried everything he owned: a copper axe, a bearskin cap, shoes stuffed with grass.
His last meal was ibex meat and fat, and flat einkorn bread, eaten high on the mountain.
Then, in the snow of the pass, an arrow found his shoulder.
The snow of the same night buried him where he fell.
Luckily, it never let him go.
The ice kept his whole daily life, his axe, his hat, his last meal, for five thousand three hundred years.
In 1991, hikers found him lying face down in the melting snow, still wearing his cap.
He set out to cross the pass. He is still there, behind glass, in Bolzano.
